_source: MNLCP 9-30-2026 FINAL (DOFAW, version 2026-09-29): Ch 4 Table 1 (p.19, lines 980-1000); Ch 5b Table 2 (pp.20-21); Ch 5e Table 4 (p.27); Ch 6a Forest Birds (pp.31-36, lines 1395-1628); Ch 6b Seabirds (pp.37-40, lines 1629-1789); Ch 6c Waterbirds (pp.41-46, lines 1790-2019); Ch 6d Terrestrial Plants (pp.47-56, lines 2020-2393); Ch 6j Tables 26-27 (pp.84-87); App 1 (pp.A1-5 to A1-6, lines 5100-5185); App 2 Tables 1-2 (pp.A2-15, A2-28 to A2-37); App 3-4. Footprint PU counts for the three bird groups are not stated in the plan and are null; plant priority footprint uses the plan body figure (155 PUs) although App 1 gives 181 (see content/notes/groups1.md).

groups.name: Forest birds
primary_threats: Introduced avian malaria transmitted by introduced Culex mosquitoes
Warming climate that lets mosquitoes and disease spread upslope
Invasive vertebrate predators (rats, cats and others)
top_actions: S15 Future tools to address avian malaria
S14 Avian disease prevention (captive bird facilities, Wolbachia releases, broadcast BTI)
S5 Terrestrial habitat management for at-risk species
Emergency: reduce mosquitoes and disease in three areas in and next to occupied East Maui habitat
Emergency: establish a second ʻākohekohe population by translocation to suitable habitat not on Maui
groups.one_line_summary: Four at-risk forest birds survive only on East Maui, two facing imminent extinction; controlling mosquito-borne avian malaria is the top priority, followed by returning birds to West Maui and Molokaʻi.

species_highlights.name: Maui parrotbill
species_highlights.note: Endangered; fewer than 150 left in about 30 km² of East Maui rainforest; faces imminent extinction. Recovery target 2,500 birds across East Maui, West Maui and Molokaʻi.

species_highlights.name: Crested honeycreeper
species_highlights.note: Endangered; 1,200-2,000 birds on Haleakalā, none in captivity; faces imminent extinction. Recovery target 7,500 birds.

species_highlights.name: ʻIʻiwi
species_highlights.note: Federally threatened; about 50,000 in Maui Nui, all on East Maui.

species_highlights.name: Maui creeper
species_highlights.note: Not listed but declining; about 99,000, all on East Maui.

groups.name: Seabirds
primary_threats: Introduced mammalian predators, especially rats, mongoose and cats
Artificial lights at night, power lines, wind turbines and roadways
top_actions: S16 Minimization and modification of infrastructure
groups.one_line_summary: Three listed seabirds nest across all four Maui Nui islands; none faces imminent extinction, and predator-proof fencing, predator control and safer infrastructure can bring them above 50 percent persistence with existing tools.

species_highlights.name: Hawaiian petrel
species_highlights.note: Endangered; endemic; about 6,100-6,750 breeding pairs, mostly East Maui and Lānaʻi. Target 18,000 pairs.

species_highlights.name: Newell's shearwater
species_highlights.note: Threatened; endemic; 102-300 breeding pairs on steep wet-to-mesic forest slopes. Target 3,600 pairs.

species_highlights.name: Band-rumped storm petrel
species_highlights.note: Hawaiʻi distinct population segment endangered; indigenous; 151-350 breeding pairs, known breeding sites extremely rare. Target 1,800 pairs.

groups.name: Waterbirds
primary_threats: Habitat loss from human modification of wetlands
Introduced mammalian predators (mongoose, cats, rats, domestic dogs)
Hybridization of kōloa maoli with feral mallards
top_actions: S16 Minimization and modification of infrastructure
Reintroduce ʻalae ʻula on Molokaʻi; control kōloa-mallard hybridization, then reintroduce kōloa maoli
groups.one_line_summary: All five native waterbirds are listed and two are gone from Maui Nui; the plan builds on past success with wetland protection, predator fencing and control, and later reintroductions.

species_highlights.name: Hawaiian coot
species_highlights.note: Endangered; 364 birds in Maui Nui. Target 750.

species_highlights.name: Hawaiian goose
species_highlights.note: Federally threatened, State endangered; 610 birds on Maui and Molokaʻi. Target 1,000, including 200 on Molokaʻi.

species_highlights.name: Hawaiian moorhen
species_highlights.note: Endangered; no longer in Maui Nui. To be reintroduced on Molokaʻi (target 250).

species_highlights.name: Hawaiian duck
species_highlights.note: Endangered; kōloa-like ducks in Maui Nui appear to be hybrids with feral mallards. Reintroduction (target 250) awaits hybridization control.

groups.name: Plants
primary_threats: Invertebrate pests: slugs (101 species), black twig borer (21), ants (7), coconut rhinoceros beetle, naio thrips
top_actions: Emergency PEPP actions for 102 species: survey, monitor, collect seeds and propagules, control local threats, propagate and outplant
S13 Future tools for rare plants and invertebrates
S5 Terrestrial habitat management for at-risk species
groups.one_line_summary: The largest group, with 197 at-risk plants and 102 facing imminent extinction; emergency PEPP work, a 317-planning-unit recovery footprint prioritized with OptimTFE and refined by experts, and new tools against pests that cannot be controlled today.

species_highlights.name: Pua ʻala
species_highlights.note: Endangered PEPP species; 7 known occupied planning units.

species_highlights.name: Kokiʻo
species_highlights.note: Endangered PEPP species with no known occupied planning units; 3 recovery planning units in the footprint.

species_highlights.name: ʻOha wai
species_highlights.note: Endangered PEPP species; 28 known occupied planning units.

species_highlights.name: Haha
species_highlights.note: Endangered; few-populations (POP) tier; 14 known occupied planning units.
